design_finding.summary: Both WHOLE-TREE-CODISPATCH and WHOLE-TREE-PHASE-EXEMPT are RED today for a DIFFERENT mechanical reason than the plan's Design Decisions section assumed. The plan assumed today's script would falsely ADMIT a disjoint-but-both-sentinel-carrying pair (no existing predicate reads the claim). In fact the EXISTING file_scope_collision exact-match branch already defers the pair today, because both candidates declare the identical literal '__WHOLE_TREE__' string and scopes_overlap_first's exact-match rule fires on identical strings regardless of slashes -- the plan's 'inert' claim for the sentinel is scoped to inertness against a REAL path, not against another instance of itself. Today's wrongness is therefore: defer fires via the WRONG defer_reason (file_scope_collision) and is missing claim_sentinel/whole_tree_claim and (for the phase-exempt case) does not honor --phase-map at all. This means Phase 4's stated mechanism ('a new dimension evaluated LAST, only on a candidate the three existing branches would otherwise ADMIT, no existing branch's code path edited') cannot work as literally written for the same-sentinel in-batch case: the exact-match scan intercepts first. Phase 4 must resolve this -- most likely by giving the whole-tree-claim check first look (or a short-circuit) specifically when the colliding file_scope entry equals the reserved sentinel, before falling through to the ordinary exact-match collision reason. Recorded via issue-record.sh (class design-gap, severity costly) and in inline comments at both fixture sites in test-orchestrate-batch-admit.sh.
design_finding.action_required_in_phase_4: Re-derive the admission-dimension placement so the whole-tree-claim check (with its own defer_reason/fields and phase exemption) takes precedence over the plain exact-match collision specifically for sentinel-vs-sentinel entries, without disturbing the exact-match branch's behavior for any real-path collision.
